blurb: Samach Vav P. 192-193: In addition (to avodah receiving support from above), the general inspiration of avodah every day is empowered by the auspicious time of Keriyas Shema and prayer each morning, which There was a mitzvah to bring the smoldering coals of the outer altar to fuel the inner altar, indicating that refining the birurim of the 288 sparks (on the outer altar) fuels the ketoros that rise from these coals, to elevate the soul higher and higher, to be absorbed in its source in the "body of the King." The divine soul's elevation comes from the work with the animal soul. Additionally, bringing the coals from the outer to the inner altar refers to "unify our hearts" -- both sides of the heart, the divine and animal soul. This avodah of the core souls comes as a gift from above, something that cannot be generated by the soul's own effort. However, to reach this level we first need to do the avodah below, to the extent that we are capable of. Then it is given the love from above -- one who toils erev Shabbos, the exertion to excite the passion of the physical heart, eats on Shabbos, receives the ahava rabba and ahava b'taanugim from above. Shemone Esrei in the daily prayer is similar to the level of Shabbos: Following the toil of refining the animal soul through the perceptible and palpable passion in Pesukei D'zimra, with sound and song, followed by the blessings before Shema and the Shema -- we reach the avodah of elevating the soul itself in the 15 vav'in of Emes V'ya
